sources_considered.why: Primary industry research on construction costs and supply constraints.
Read successfully, but its 2026-wide findings do not isolate conditions before the July post or supply the missing lifecycle calculation.
Primary research illustrates why token prices and costs per completed task can move differently. It does not measure infrastructure investment recovery.

evidence_items.explanation: The report documents construction inflation and a premium for AI facilities. It supports a cost-pressure mechanism, but differences in size and specifications do not establish that elapsed buildout itself raises comparable costs or required lifetime returns.

The study identifies falling token prices alongside rising token consumption. This is a material qualification to a blanket cost-escalation reading, but it measures inference pricing rather than construction, financing or investment recovery.

unresolved_gaps: No matched project series isolates the effect of continued AI buildout on all-in costs.
No lifecycle calculation connects the measured cost changes to the required payoff.
Construction costs and inference prices measure different things and cannot be combined into a decisive score.
